files.lesson.md: --- order: 25 unit: trig9 node: AC9M9M03 n2 uses: [AC9M9M03 n1] assumes: [AC9M9M03 n1] connection: ramp-1-in-14 title: Find an angle summary: "When you know two sides and want the angle, use the inverse ratio: tan⁻¹, sin⁻¹ or cos⁻¹ turn a ratio back into an angle." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A ramp rises 1 m over 14 m of ground. How steep is that, in degrees?" app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8377 url: http://127.0.0.1:8377/index.html readySelector: "#board" layout: full --- Ramps for wheelchairs must be gentle. Australian Standards allow ramps up to 9 m long a slope of at most 1 in 14 ([Queensland Health](https://www.health.qld.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0029/1477208/Ramps-to-the-house-and-slopes-in-the-garden-slides.pdf)). A ramp rises 1 m for every 14 m along the ground. What angle does it make with the ground? Have a guess, and we'll come back to it at the end. ## Predict: how steep ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to a size for the 1 in 14 angle shows whether students expect a gentle ramp to be small in degrees." check: type: predict q: "A ramp rises 1 m over a run of 14 m. About how big is its angle with the ground?" options: - "About 4°" - "About 14°" - "About 7°" - "About 45°" actual: "About 4°. A ramp can be very gentle: 1 m up over 14 m along is only 4.1°. 45° would be 1 up for every 1 along." ``` ## Run: set the angle ```step stage: run insight: "Tangent of the angle is rise ÷ run, so the angle is the number whose tangent is 1 ÷ 14." try: { playground: board, starter: "angle.yml#run", height: 560 } check: { type: board, text: "Set $t$ to $4$. Read $\\tan 4°$. Is it close to $1 \\div 14 = 0.071$?", when: "t = 4" } ``` ## Investigate: the inverse ratio ```step stage: investigate insight: "tan turns an angle into a ratio; tan⁻¹ turns a ratio back into an angle. The ratio goes into the inverse key, not the plain one." tasks: - check: type: number q: "The ramp has opposite $= 1$ and adjacent $= 14$. What is the ratio $1 \\div 14$ to 3 decimal places?" answer: 0.071 tolerance: 0.001 explain: "1 ÷ 14 = 0.0714." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is $1 \\div 14$ to 3 decimal places?", answer: 0.071, tolerance: 0.001, explain: "1 ÷ 14 = 0.0714." } - check: type: number q: "Use $\\tan^{-1}$ on $0.5$ (opposite $=$ 1, adjacent $= 2$). What is the angle, to the nearest degree?" answer: 27 tolerance: 0.6 explain: "tan⁻¹ 0.5 = 26.6°, about 27°." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#sam" text: "Sam finds the angle of the ramp. Click the line where his working goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: trig-inverse-missed explain: "Line 3: tan 0.071 would be an angle's tangent, not an angle. Use tan⁻¹ 0.071 to turn the ratio into an angle." ``` ### Ratio to angle ```worked \tan\theta = \dfrac{1}{14} :: Rise is opposite, run is adjacent. \tan\theta = 0.0714 :: Divide. \theta = \tan^{-1}(0.0714) :: Use the inverse key. \theta \approx 4.1° :: The ramp is about 4°. ``` ### The inverse key ### Find the mistake Read Sam's working. Which line forgets the inverse? ## Modify: other angles ```step stage: modify insight: "Changing which two sides are known tests the choice of inverse ratio." tasks: - hint: ["Opposite 3, adjacent 4: tangent.", "tan⁻¹(3 ÷ 4)."] check: { type: number, q: "A triangle has opposite $3$ and adjacent $4$. What is the angle, to the nearest degree?", answer: 37, tolerance: 0.6, explain: "tan⁻¹ 0.75 = 36.9°, about 37°." } - hint: ["Adjacent and hypotenuse: cosine.", "cos⁻¹(1 ÷ 4)."] check: { type: number, q: "A $4$ m ladder has its foot $1$ m from the wall. What angle does the ladder make with the ground, to the nearest degree?", answer: 76, tolerance: 0.6, explain: "cos⁻¹ 0.25 = 75.5°, about 76°." } - hint: ["Check which side is the hypotenuse.", "The hypotenuse is the longest side."] check: { type: question, q: "A student uses $\\sin^{-1}(7 \\div 5)$ and gets an error. Why?", options: ["Sine can't be more than 1: the opposite side can't be longer than the hypotenuse", "The calculator is broken", "They should use tangent", "7 is too big"], answer: 0, feedback: [null, "The calculator is right: no such angle.", "The sides given suit sine or tan; the issue is the order.", "The size of 7 isn't the problem."], explain: "The hypotenuse is the longest side, so opposite ÷ hypotenuse is below 1. Put the hypotenuse underneath." } ``` ### A 3-4 triangle ### A ladder ### An error ## Practise: find the angle ```step stage: practise insight: "Choosing the ratio from the two sides known, then using its inverse." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A triangle has opposite 5 and adjacent 5. What is the angle?" answer: 45 tolerance: 0.5 explain: "tan⁻¹ 1 = 45°." - check: type: number q: "A triangle has opposite 6 and hypotenuse 10. What is the angle to the nearest degree?" answer: 37 tolerance: 0.6 explain: "sin⁻¹ 0.6 = 36.9°, about 37°." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is $6 \\div 10$?", answer: 0.6, tolerance: 0.001, explain: "6 ÷ 10 = 0.6." } - check: type: number q: "Review: a tree's top is 20 m above your eye and you are 20 m away. What is the angle?" answer: 45 tolerance: 0.5 explain: "tan⁻¹(20 ÷ 20) = 45°." ``` ### Opposite and adjacent ### Opposite and hypotenuse ### Review ## Make: is the ramp allowed ```step stage: make insight: "Returning to the ramp: turn the rise and run into an angle and compare with the 1 in 14 limit." tasks: - hint: ["Rise and run: tan⁻¹.", "Compare 0.6 ÷ 8 with 1 ÷ 14."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A ramp rises 0.6 m over a run of 8 m. What angle does it make with the ground? The 1 in 14 limit is 4.1°. (1 decimal place. The ramp is made up for the task.)" steps: - ["$\\tan\\theta = 0.6 \\div 8 = 0.075$", "rise over run"] - ["$\\theta = \\tan^{-1}(0.075)$", "use the inverse key"] - ["$4.3°$", "bigger than 4.1°, so too steep"] answer: "4.3" answerLabel: "Angle (degrees)" tolerance: 0.1 feedback: - ["0.075", "That's the ratio. Use tan⁻¹ to get the angle."] - ["0.0752", "That's the ratio. Use tan⁻¹ to get the angle."] criteria: - "I used rise ÷ run." - "I used the inverse key." - "I compared with 4.1°." explain: "tan⁻¹ 0.075 = 4.29°, about 4.3°: slightly steeper than the 4.1° limit." - check: type: question q: "Is a ramp with an angle of 4.3° allowed if the limit is 4.1°?" options: ["No: it's steeper than the limit", "Yes: it's close enough", "Yes: 4.3 is bigger", "Can't tell"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The rule is a limit, not a guide.", "A bigger angle is steeper, which is worse.", "You compare the angles."] explain: "A bigger angle is steeper. The ramp would need to be longer." ``` ### The angle ### Allowed? The limit is for ramps up to 9 m long: shorter or longer ramps have other rules ([Queensland Health](https://www.health.qld.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0029/1477208/Ramps-to-the-house-and-slopes-in-the-garden-slides.pdf)). The 0.6 m ramp is made up for the task. **Also used in** - **Building.** Roof pitch and stair slope in degrees. - **Navigation.** The angle to steer to reach a place. - **Next lesson.** Similar triangles and scale. ```teacher summary: Students use tan⁻¹, sin⁻¹ and cos⁻¹ to find an unknown angle from two sides (AC9M9M03, node 2). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 8 min · Practise and Make 12 min goals: - I can pick the ratio from the two sides I know. - I can use the inverse key to find the angle. - I can check the angle makes sense. struggle: "Using tan instead of tan⁻¹. Ask: are you going from angle to ratio, or ratio to angle?" before: > Students need Find a side with trigonometry. The one idea: the inverse key undoes the ratio. Check the calculator is in degree mode. The 1 in 14 limit applies to ramps up to 9 m (AS 1428.1, via the Queensland Health slides). The 0.6 m ramp is made up for the task. running: - "Predict: show of hands before the board." - "Paper: the ramp angle in Make is worked on paper first." stuck: - see: A student gets 0.07° for the ramp. ask: Did you use the inverse key? fix: tan⁻¹ turns the ratio into the angle. stretch: What angle is a 1 in 8 ramp, and which kind of ramp is it? support: A printed card with the three inverse keys and the sides each uses. leads: | Continues AC9M9M03 node 2. Where it leads: Similar triangles, scale and proportion. exit: q: tan of an angle is 1. What is the angle? a: 45°. explain: | tan⁻¹, sin⁻¹ and cos⁻¹ turn a ratio back into an angle. Name the sides, pick the ratio, then use its inverse. ```

files.working.txt:
# Sam's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: sam
The ramp rises 1 m over a run of 14 m. I want the angle.
tan(angle) = 1 ÷ 14 = 0.071.
So the angle = tan 0.071 = 0.07°.
# endregion
